answer: Per-identity cost mirroring. Each new identity's ongoing compute quota is set by a kernel that samples its earliest interactions, so a clone must sustain the same costly narrow behaviour as the original. An atlas of these quota traces is shared across agents, letting honest agents cheaply prove a long low-variance history. A plume of cheap identities diverges fast and gets throttled, forcing the attacker to pay full quota upkeep per clone indefinitely.
